terminal_record.title: Unverified Claim of an April 2025 Family-Separation Reinstatement
terminal_record.description_short: The supplied record alleges an April 2025 return to family separation; packet sources describe detention or deportation and do not verify that claim.
terminal_record.description_medium: The frozen synopsis alleges that the administration reinstated zero-tolerance family separation on April 1, 2025, separating thousands of parents and children and prosecuting parents. The packet does not establish those claims. Its AP item concerns Alien Enemies Act deportation flights, while the April Guardian report describes family detention, a distinct practice. The allegations remain unverified and are retained only for internal drafting.
terminal_record.description_long: The frozen synopsis alleges that the Trump administration reinstated its 2018 zero-tolerance family-separation policy on April 1, 2025. It claims that parents and children were deliberately separated as a deterrence measure, that thousands of families were affected, and that parents faced criminal prosecution. It further attributes an acknowledgment of intentional separation to the administration and says pediatricians and child-welfare experts warned of psychological harm. These are supplied allegations, not established findings in this packet. The AP source concerns Alien Enemies Act deportation flights. The April Guardian report describes family detention at Karnes and Dilley; detention does not establish that parents and children were separated from one another. The packet contains no same-event source confirming formal reinstatement, separations, the quantity, prosecution, attributed acknowledgment, or the quoted expert response. This internal draft keeps the supplied account visible for reconciliation while marking every central allegation unverified. It does not treat detention or deportation as proof of the claimed separation policy, and it does not assign an impact score to an unestablished event.
